touches.text: A device talks to other devices only over the bus, never by importing them.
The exceptions are client tools a device publishes:

System: a box has to name itself before any bus is up (a saveslate, an install), so the system device publishes the host's name and OS family (6.6.3.7). - akiendelllinux_cc_0 2.3.8Every device has the panes the base shim defines (17.1.3.5.2), drawn by the web server (15):
It launches each device's cairn/devices/<device>/groundloop/pulse.py, each as its own process (5.8.3.4).
pulse.py is part of the shim. The ground loop calling it tells the shim the pulse has arrived, and starts the shim if it isn't running.

The hostname comes from the system device. It answers which box (the short hostname, lowercased) and which OS family, and nothing else in Cairn asks the OS for the hostname. Callers reach it through the client tool it publishes (2.3.7.1.5), so a box names itself on every OS, Windows included, with no bus running. - akiendelllinux_cc_0

A client tool a device publishes (2.3.7.1) is not the general case: it is the device's own interface, made for other components to use, so it lives with its device (cairn/devices/<d>/tools/<t>/, published_by_device). Scratch bus, the database client, the trouble store, the librarian's trees and the system device's host tool all live there. CC's decision, from 2.3.7.1 and Akien's "hostname should come from the system device" (2026-11-21). - akiendelllinux_cc_0

RULE 1, ENCAPSULATION: every component talks to every other only through that component's public interface: a device's is the bus plus any client tool it publishes; a machine's or tool's is what its entry declares. Nothing outside a device reaches into its code, skills included. A ticket builds inside its own component, and its proofs measure only that component. WHY: it limits a change to the component that made it.

Every device has a shim. Each shim is its own process, one per instance, and connects to the bus as a client. WHY: in the bus process, updating one shim meant bringing the whole bus down, and one shim's stall was everyone's. Separate, a shim restarts itself when its own files change, like the ground loop, and the bus stays up.

The ground loop finds one pulse.py per device. pulse.py reads its own device's declared instances (5.7.3.4) and pulses each one, so the ground loop never needs to know instances exist. Pulsing an instance that isn't connected is what starts its shim.

pulse.py asks nobody anything. It starts the shim if it's down, else tells the mechanisms inside the shim that need a pulse "here ya go!" Only daemon-shaped things hang there, things that actually need a heartbeat (eg cc's Gmail fetch, 10.3.6); everything else fires on events. WHY: pulse.py is a place to hang daemons from, not managers.
Physics: the encapsulation_holds sieve in build_inspector, a device-path check. Code in device bar may not import cairn.devices.foo except a tool foo publishes. Inside one device nothing is checked.
